Review date: 2026-08-09. Package version reviewed: TaxaWizard 0.1.0. Review conducted by
Claude Code, using the template in `inst/Code and Domain Review 2.Rmd` (the TaxaID-root
copy). This is TaxaWizard's first full code + domain review -- every other package in the
ecosystem already had one. This review combines findings and fixes in one pass (no
separate response document), matching the convention already used for
`TaxaFetch`/`TaxaLikely`/`TaxaMatch`/`TaxaFlag`.

`devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes (unchanged -- was already clean).
`devtools::test()`: 696 expectations (up from 655 before this review), 0 failures.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: The code is readable, organized, and efficient.

Readable and consistently organized across all 11 `R/` files -- roxygen documentation,
`.`-prefixed internal helpers, and `package::function()` cross-package calls follow the
same conventions used throughout the rest of the ecosystem. `R/shiny.R` (1671 lines) is
by far the largest file, but that reflects real, non-duplicated surface area (script
parsing via `parse()`/`getSrcref()`, two independent annotation modes, and a full
UI+server code generator for the produced `app.R`) rather than disorganization -- it is
internally well-sectioned (`Script Parsing` / `Generic Script Segmentation` / `Script
Annotation` / `App Code Generation`) with clear boundaries between sections.

TaxaWizard is architecturally the most unusual package in the ecosystem: it doesn't
compute anything biological itself -- it generates R code that calls the other eight
packages. The "graph-constrained LLM" design (`R/graph.R`'s `.compute_paths()` computing
valid pipeline paths in R so the LLM only classifies/selects/parameterizes, never invents
function names) is a sound way to keep an LLM from hallucinating call sequences, and is
implemented consistently across all three phases.

One real base-R name collision found and fixed: `.subset_for_trial(df, n, by)` (`R/trial.R`,
internal-only) used `df` as its first parameter name, shadowing `stats::df()` -- the one
function in the package still carrying the exact pattern every other package in this
ecosystem has already fixed (`TaxaTools::create_taxon_names()`'s `df` -> `input_df`,
`TaxaFlag`'s four-function fix, etc.). Renamed to `input_df`; zero external impact since
the function is `@noRd` and every existing call site (tests) passes it positionally.

### [x] Optimizations: No performance concerns; one real functional gap found and fixed.

Nothing in this package does bulk/iterative computation at a scale where an algorithmic
change would matter -- `.compute_paths()`'s backward search + Cartesian product of
multi-input plans is over a graph with a few dozen nodes/edges, not user data.

**Real gap: `.generate_app()` was a hardcoded placeholder ("Full implementation
forthcoming"), while a complete, working app generator (`workflow_app()`/
`.build_app_code()`) already existed in the same package.** `.generate_outputs()` (the
dispatcher a completed `workflow_engine()` interview calls) routed any response with
`"app"` in `dag$outputs` to the placeholder, not to `workflow_app()` -- so if an
interview ever produced `outputs = c("script", "app")` (a value the legacy
`system_prompt.md` schema explicitly documents as valid, even though the currently-active
`phase_parameterize.md` prompt instead tells the LLM to point users at
`workflow_app()` as a separate follow-up call), the user would have silently received a
non-functional stub `app.R` instead of a real one. In practice the live prompt makes this
path unlikely to be reached today, but the landmine was real and the fix was
straightforward: `.generate_app()` now delegates to `workflow_app(script_path = ...,
launch = FALSE)` whenever a sibling script was generated in the same response, falling
back to a (now honestly-worded, pointing the user at `workflow_app()`) placeholder only
when no script is available. See `R/output.R`.

### [x] Coding standards: Two real issues found and fixed; otherwise clean.

Every exported function (`workflow_create()`, `workflow_engine()`, `workflow_fix()`,
`workflow_app()`, `annotate_script()`, plus the two deprecated wrappers) has complete
roxygen with `@param` for every argument, an accurate `@return`, and runnable
`@examples` (correctly wrapped in `\dontrun{}` where they require API access or an
interactive session).

**Real bug: `lifecycle::badge("deprecated")` used in roxygen but `lifecycle` was
declared nowhere in `DESCRIPTION`.** `R/cli.R` and `R/gadget.R` both use
`` `r lifecycle::badge("deprecated")` `` in their `@description` blocks -- this is a live
inline-R roxygen2 expression (confirmed by inspecting the built `man/workflow_chat.Rd`/
`man/workflow_gadget.Rd`, which contain the expanded `\ifelse{html}{...lifecycle-deprecated.svg...}`
markup, not the literal backtick-r text), evaluated at `devtools::document()` time. A
contributor running `document()` for the first time on a machine without `lifecycle`
already installed (e.g. as a transitive dependency of something else) would hit an
opaque failure with no clue why, since neither `Imports` nor `Suggests` mentioned it.
Fixed by adding `lifecycle` to `Suggests`.

**Inconsistency: `workflow_engine()`/`.call_llm()` defaulted to a different model than
every user-facing wrapper.** `R/api.R`'s `.call_llm()` and `R/engine.R`'s
`workflow_engine()` both defaulted `model = "claude-opus-4-6"`, while
`workflow_create()`, `workflow_chat()`, and `workflow_gadget()` all default to
`"claude-sonnet-4-6"` -- and this package's own `CLAUDE.md` documents Sonnet as the
intended engine default ("Sonnet is faster and cheaper for the interview loop; the code
comes from pre-validated snippets, not the LLM"). A caller using `workflow_engine()`
directly (the natural entry point for scripting/testing, and the one this review's own
example runner script uses) silently got a different, undocumented default. Fixed by
aligning both to `"claude-sonnet-4-6"`.

**Minor DRY nit, fixed:** `R/graph.R`'s `.build_phase_prompt()` (`path_select` branch)
called `sub("{{INPUT_TYPE}}", ...)` immediately followed by `gsub("{{INPUT_TYPE}}", ...)`
on the identical pattern/replacement (same for `{{OUTPUT_TYPE}}`) -- the `sub()` calls
were fully redundant, since the following `gsub()` already replaces every occurrence
including the first. Removed the two dead `sub()` lines.

**Package hygiene: three orphaned data files and a `.DS_Store` were bundled into every
install.** `inst/goby_priors.rds`, `inst/gobiidae_priors.rds`, and
`inst/tidewater_goby_priors.rds` (~120KB combined, dated May 7, real
`TaxaExpect`-style prior tables from what appears to be a one-off manual test session)
had zero references anywhere in `R/`, `tests/`, or `inst/` -- confirmed via a full-package
grep before removing them. A package whose own stated purpose has no data dependencies
(`workflow_engine(history, metadata) -> JSON`; metadata comes from `inst/metadata/*.json`)
should not ship unrelated species-specific prior tables in every tarball. Also removed
`tests/.DS_Store` (a macOS Finder artifact; already covered by `.gitignore` going forward,
so this was a stale tracked file rather than a gitignore gap).

### [x] Automated tests: Confirmed passing when run locally; real coverage gaps found and partly closed.

`devtools::test()`: 696 expectations, 0 failures (up from 655).

**Coverage gap, largely closed this session:** before this review, only 3 of 11 `R/`
files had a dedicated test file (`engine.R`, `graph.R`, `shiny.R`) -- `api.R`,
`metadata.R`, `context.R`, `create.R`, `output.R`, `cli.R`, `trial.R`, `gadget.R`, `zzz.R`
had none. The highest-value gap was `R/output.R`'s `.generate_script()`/
`.append_to_script()` -- the actual code-generation logic that produces the package's
core deliverable (the self-contained `.R` workflow script) -- which had zero test
coverage despite being exercised by every real `workflow_create()` session. Added
`tests/testthat/test-output.R` (fresh-script header/params/steps, the one-step-only
debug-mode subsetting placement, `.find_existing_script()`'s date-scoping,
`.append_to_script()`'s step renumbering + single-footer invariant + `total_steps`
update, `.generate_markdown()`, `.generate_outputs()`'s `appended` attribute, and the
`.generate_app()` fallback fixed above). Also added two `.parse_engine_response()` tests
in `test-engine.R` covering the previously-untested "Approach 3" brace-matching fallback
(LLM prose before the JSON object; multiple top-level JSON blocks, picking the one with a
`status` field) -- this is the mechanism that keeps a malformed/chatty LLM response from
crashing the conversation, and it was the one branch of that function's three-tier
fallback with no test at all.

**Still open, not attempted this session (flagged, not fixed):** `api.R`'s
non-Anthropic provider bridge inside `.call_llm()` (lines ~34-63 -- building a
`llm_fn` wrapper around `TaxaTools::call_api` when `TaxaID.provider` is set to a
non-Anthropic value) has no test coverage; `metadata.R`, `context.R`, `cli.R`'s
`.parse_error_context()`, and `create.R`'s console/viewer loops also remain untested.
None of these showed a defect during manual reading, but a full closure of this gap
is future work, not part of this pass.

### [x] Vulnerabilities: Two real issues found and fixed.

**Real vulnerability: `eval(parse(text = input$...))` on a Shiny input in every generated
app, with no server-side validation.** `.param_assembly_line()`'s `function_ref` branch
(`R/shiny.R`) generated code of the form `assign(nm, eval(parse(text = input$param_llm_fn)),
envir = env)` in the produced `app.R`. The corresponding widget is a `selectInput()`
constrained to six hardcoded provider choices, but that constraint is UI-only -- Shiny's
client/server protocol does not stop a browser client from sending an arbitrary
`input$...` value via `Shiny.setInputValue()` in the browser console/devtools, regardless
of what the rendered widget offers. Since `workflow_app()`'s own documentation explicitly
positions generated apps as something to be "shared with collaborators" (i.e., a
multi-user, potentially internet-facing deployment target, not a single-user local
script), this was a real, if narrow, remote-code-execution vector: any user of a deployed
app could get arbitrary R code evaluated server-side. Fixed by extracting the six allowed
provider strings into a single shared source (`.llm_provider_choices()`, used by both the
widget builder and the server code generator so the two can't drift), and by emitting an
explicit allow-list check (`if (!.fn_str %in% .allowed_fns) stop(...)`) before the
`eval(parse(...))` call in every generated app. New tests in `test-shiny.R` confirm the
allow-list check is present in the generated code and that it actually blocks a tampered
value (simulated via a non-widget input string) before `eval()` would run it.

**Real hygiene issue: API keys persisted to disk in plaintext with default file
permissions.** `.save_session()` (`R/cli.R`) `saveRDS()`s the full conversation state --
including `api_key` and `llm_fn` (which, for a non-Anthropic provider, is typically a
closure that itself captures an API key in its enclosing environment; this package's own
`@param llm_fn` documentation for `workflow_create()` shows exactly this pattern for
Azure) -- to `file.path(tempdir(), "taxawizard_session.rds")`, so that `workflow_fix()`
can resume the conversation later. This is necessary for the error-fix feature to work at
all, and `tempdir()` is process-private on most systems, but the file was written with
whatever the process's default `umask` produces, not explicitly restricted. Fixed by
calling `Sys.chmod(session_path, mode = "0600")` immediately after `saveRDS()`, so the
session file (and the secrets inside it) is readable only by the owning user regardless
of the environment's default permissions.

Everything else checked came back clean: the Shiny gadget's chat rendering
(`R/create.R`'s `.create_viewer()`) HTML-escapes all message text on both the client
(inline JS) and server (the `observe()` block building `update_chat` HTML) before
insertion, so neither the user's own typed input nor the LLM's response can inject
markup into the chat log. `.generate_script()`'s path handling escapes embedded quotes
before building string literals rather than concatenating raw user paths into R source
unescaped, and `workflow_app()`'s file-path replacement in step code uses
`fixed = TRUE` throughout (no accidental regex interpretation of user-supplied file
paths).

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available. Review
should be conducted by someone with applicable subject-matter knowledge.

### [x] Scientific Rigor

TaxaWizard does not itself perform any biological computation -- it interviews the user,
selects a path through the ecosystem's existing (already-reviewed) statistical
components, and fills in pre-written code snippets with the user's parameter values. Its
own "correctness" is therefore about faithfully reproducing what the underlying TaxaID
packages already do, not about any biological claim of its own. The one place this
distinction could matter is if `inst/metadata/*.json` (the parameter documentation
surfaced to the LLM and, indirectly, to the user) drifted from what the real functions
actually do or require -- but that risk is already the subject of a separate, extensive,
actively-maintained audit process (`diagnostics/taxawizard_metadata_audit.R`, run
repeatedly per this package's own `CLAUDE.md` session notes, most recently 2026-08-09) and
was deliberately out of scope for this code-focused pass to avoid duplicating that work.

### [x] Outputs

Not directly applicable -- TaxaWizard's own output is generated R source code (a `.R`
script, a `.md` methods file, or an `app.R`), not a scientific result. The generated
script's own outputs are whatever the selected TaxaID functions produce, unchanged by
TaxaWizard.

### [x] Algorithms

The one algorithm genuinely internal to this package -- `.compute_paths()`'s backward
recursive graph search with Cartesian-product combination for multi-input edges -- is a
standard, appropriate technique for the problem (enumerate all ways to reach a target
node from a start node in a small DAG with cycle prevention via `visited_targets`), and
is exercised heavily by `test-graph.R`. No domain-specific (biological) algorithm choices
are made in this package.

# File specific comments

**R/api.R** -- `.call_llm()`'s non-Anthropic bridge (auto-detecting `TaxaID.provider` and
wrapping `TaxaTools::call_api`) duplicates logic conceptually similar to
`TaxaWizard::.onAttach()` (`R/zzz.R`) and to `TaxaTools`'s own provider auto-detection --
by design, since `TaxaWizard` deliberately has no hard `Imports` dependency on
`TaxaTools` (Suggests only), this can't be factored into one shared helper without
creating that dependency. Left as-is; the duplication is small and the design constraint
is documented.

**R/output.R** -- `.generate_script()`/`.append_to_script()` both duplicate the
"indent code inside `quote({...})`, wrap in `.run_step()`" step-formatting logic. A
shared internal helper (e.g. `.format_step_lines(step, step_num)`) would remove the
duplication; not extracted in this pass since both call sites are short and the tests
added this session cover both paths' current behavior, but worth doing if a third
call site is ever added.

**R/shiny.R** -- `.classify_param()`'s file-input/file-output detection
(`grepl('^".*\\.(csv|tsv|txt|rds|xlsx|fasta|fa)"', ...)` vs. the output variant's
`grepl("output|save|write", name, ...)`) is a reasonable heuristic for TaxaWizard's own
generated scripts (which always name output-path parameters predictably, e.g.
`output_path`/`save_path`), but would misclassify a generic script's parameter named
something like `write_up_notes_path` (a real file path, not an output path, containing
"write"). This only affects `annotate_script(mode = "self"/"llm")`'s automatic
classification for arbitrary user scripts, not TaxaWizard's own generated scripts, and
the self-guided mode already lets the user correct misclassified parameters
interactively -- not changed, but worth knowing if `.classify_param()` is ever reused for
a fully-automatic (no human confirmation) path.
